analyticalQuestion: Can the R0.29 canonical factorization replace the exact R0.41 direct-transport norm barrier, certify the preassigned r=0.282 acceptance point, and raise the reduced-system common radius while retaining all input degrees and charges?
supportedClaim: For the canonical stretch operator S_a=L^(-1){a,.}, the weighted monomial column factor is |i(s/j)-q|/3. The output-degree divisor cancels exactly, leaving no input-degree prefactor. Convexity on the genuine common slope interval [-1,2] therefore reduces every polynomial column to the two endpoints, while the active tail has exact endpoint multipliers 1 and 163/243. Combined with the R0.41 all-order active restart, this proves the reduced canonical fields at r=329/1000. The old direct transport norm is already 1.0003750451629853 at r=0.282, whereas the equivalent stretch bound is 0.5817058427617202. At r=0.330 the present active-tail sufficient inequality is 1.002872150853994 and fails; the degree-80 polynomial stretch remains only a diagnostic there.

chartContract.takeaway: Canonical stretch removes the exact one-step direct-transport barrier: r=0.282 passes, and the reduced canonical fields are certified at r=0.329. The next millesimal point fails the inherited large-charge active-tail inequality rather than the displayed polynomial stretch diagnostic.

The theorem covers every input degree and charge through convex endpoint reduction and analytic tail multipliers; the five finite columns are implementation regressions only.
